newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: INTERVIEW - Portuguese investment funds see growth.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Portuguese investment funds see growth.

text.p: Assets other than real estate under management by Portuguese investment funds rose 10.5 percent in the first quarter of the year to 2.9 trillion escudos, with the stock market increasing its share, Jose Carlos Maia, the chairman of Portugal's Fund Management Association said.
Total assets were expected to rise to four trillion escudos by the end of the year from 3.1 trillion at the end of 1996, he told Reuters in an interview. In 1996, total growth had been 22 percent.
In the first quarter of the year, investment on the stock market had grown 65 percent to 143 billion escudos after rising 140 percent in the whole of 1996.

Investment in the money market, which dipped five percent in 1996, rose in the first quarter 8.8 percent to 867 billion escudos, while bond and mixed funds climbed 3.8 percent to 1.47 trillion, he said.
He said that in bonds, the fixed-rate sector grew the most, reflecting falling yields and the sharp rise in prices, particularly in January.
Fixed-rate funds, which rose 10.5 percent during the first quarter, were likely to become increasingly dominant in bond market investment, he said.
"Traditionally, we invested in index-linked...but this sector is shrinking as our financial system becomes more international," he said.
Maia, who is chief executive of Caixagest, part of the Caixa Geral de Depositos group, said that he expected the Lisbon bourse to be volatile in the coming months.
"We are going to see some volatility...and volatility can be good if you get the market timing right," he said.
Maia said that investment funds were becoming active users of the Oporto derivatives market, with the PSI20 contract on the stock index taking the lion's share.
He said that investment funds probably accounted for five percent of derivatives' turnover in March.
